chosen.premise: Rhyhorn starts charging with a goal, then forgets that goal while running because it can remember only one thing.
chosen.hook: Rhyhorn forgets why it started charging.
chosen.visualIdea: A thought bubble shows a target, vanishes mid-charge, and is replaced by a confused Rhyhorn smashing forward.
chosen.note: A concrete, unusually memorable contradiction: immense physical force paired with forgetting why it started. Multiple entries directly support the memory failure.

candidates.premise: Rhyhorn evolves into Rhydon at level 42, but reaching Rhyperior requires a trade while holding Protector.
candidates.hook: Rhyhorn's final evolution needs both level 42 and a trade.
candidates.visualIdea: Build the three-stage chain, stamp 'LEVEL 42' on the first arrow, then add a trade window and Protector.
candidates.note: The exact evolution requirements are well supported and highly visual, but evolution-method trivia is less uniquely compelling than Rhyhorn's behavioral contradiction.

candidates.premise: Rhyhorn can topple buildings and shatter mountains, yet its slow wits make it unable to help people work.
candidates.hook: Rhyhorn can destroy a mountain—but can't help at work.
candidates.visualIdea: Split the screen: Rhyhorn demolishes a building on one side, then fails at a simple construction task on the other.
candidates.note: Excellent contrast and hook, but the cited entries support building-toppling and inability to help with work—not the mountain claim in the premise.

candidates.premise: Rhyhorn cannot stop on its own; it only halts when its unstoppable charge hits something.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Rhyhorn charging toward barriers labeled 'stop,' smashing through them, then finally stopping at one.
candidates.note: Highly distinctive and visually clear, but the cited entries describe nonstop charging and straight-line movement; the explicit collision-stopping claim appears in Legends: Arceus, which is not cited.

candidates.premise: Rhyhorn's four short legs make turning so difficult that it can only charge and run in one direction.
candidates.hook: Rhyhorn can charge—but it basically can't turn.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate Rhyhorn on a straight track while arrows for left and right bend uselessly away from its path.
candidates.note: Precisely supported and easy to animate, though the premise is somewhat less surprising and visually dramatic than Rhyhorn forgetting its objective.

candidates.premise: Rhyhorn's destructive power escalates from trailer-knocking tackles to bones 1,000 times harder than human bones.
candidates.hook: Rhyhorn's bones are 1,000 times harder than ours.
candidates.visualIdea: Scale up targets from a trailer to steel to a mountain, ending with the mountain shattering on impact.
candidates.note: The bone statistic and mountain feat are striking, but the cited evidence supports them as separate claims and does not establish a clear escalation from trailer to mountain.

rounds.request: Stronger angles would need one sharply defined contradiction or rule, direct support from the cited entries, and a visual payoff that does not add unsupported feats or assumptions.
